svg.title: One number turns a circle into a beam
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch contrasting Dijkstra's search, drawn as concentric red circles spreading in every direction from the start and past the goal after expanding 1,177,499 cells, with A star's search drawn as an ellipse stretched toward the goal expanding 792,399 cells, 1.49 times fewer; the formula f of n equals g of n plus h of n highlighted with g annotated as the known cost so far and h as a guess that must not overestimate, ringed in red; and a three-node counterexample where Dijkstra finalises node B at cost one before discovering a minus-ten edge that makes the true cost minus five, with the earlier decision struck through.
svg.text: One number turns a circle into a beam
Dijkstra has no idea where the goal is
1.04 s · it looked everywhere, including behind you
A* adds ONE number: a guess of what's left
0.87 s · 1200x1200 grid, 20% blocked, both found cost 2398
and A* still returns - it just
and why it cannot handle a negative edge
Dijkstra finalises B at cost 1. FINAL.
-5 < 1. It already committed. It cannot take it back.
-> use Bellman-Ford, and pay O(VE) for the privilege
...week 25: beam search is this skeleton with no admissible h
